chapters.title: Growth is broader than promotion
chapters.lede: Career Growth explains how people grow in the network — deeper expertise, mentoring, leadership or a network role — and how a move into an approved role is decided fairly.

blocks.lead: A strong teacher can grow **without becoming a manager**. Expertise and leadership are different forms of growth, and not every excellent teacher should become a Principal.
points: **Two controlled documents** govern everything: the **Framework** (the rules) and the **Role Register** (approved roles, levels, hours, allowances).
Old job descriptions are **superseded** — where they conflict, the two controlled documents win.
Appointment follows **readiness and organisational need**, never time served alone.
No role, level, allowance, teaching-hour reduction or reporting authority may be **self-activated**.
check: A strong teacher can grow without becoming a manager
No role, level, allowance, teaching-hour reduction, or reporting authority may be self-activated
Time served alone does not create entitlement to a new role

blocks.title: What never counts as promotion evidence
blocks.text: Coaching, induction notes, mentoring records and visiting **Subject Specialist observations** stay developmental — they are **never** turned into a promotion score. Formal appraisal evidence **may** support a decision, but strong appraisal alone creates no entitlement. EASE Academic results stay protected. Personality labels such as **MBTI** must not be used for recruitment, appraisal, ranking or promotion.

chapters.title: Five parallel tracks
chapters.lede: People can move between tracks, but it is never automatic. Each track grows a different kind of strength.

rows: **Teaching & Instructional Leadership**
Teacher → Experienced Teacher → Mentor / Instructional Coach → Expert Teacher / Subject Leadership
Strong classroom practice, mentoring and curriculum expertise — **without** administrative management
**School Leadership**
Teacher → Coordinator / Head of Department → Academic Coordinator / Vice Principal → Principal
Leading people, systems, curriculum, resources and school improvement
**Student Support & Wellbeing**
Homeroom / student support → Guidance, college counselling, family, dormitory leadership → senior student-support leadership
Welfare, guidance, family partnership and post-school pathways
**Network Academic Leadership**
Strong Teacher / HOD → Subject Specialist (Eduversal) → Academic Board → wider network leadership / CAO
A network appointment track — not an entitlement, and Specialists never line-manage school HODs
**Specialist & Technical**
Deeper certification → senior specialist → coordination or functional leadership
Technical depth; roles not in the Role Register are reference only
check: Eduversal uses parallel career tracks. Movement between tracks is possible, but it is never automatic
it does not make Subject Specialists the line managers of school HODs

blocks.lead: Every role draws on the same seven competencies, at the level the role needs.
points: **Impact on Learning / Service** — visible improvement, not activity counts

blocks.title: One school reporting line
blocks.text: **FR/GM → Principal → Academic Coordinator / Vice Principal → HOD / Subject Leader → Teacher.** The CAO, Academic Board and Subject Specialists set network standards and coach — they **do not replace** the school reporting chain.

chapters.title: How a move into a new role is decided
chapters.lede: Every appointment passes the same seven gates, in order. Years of service, informal influence or training alone never skip a gate.

blocks.title: Seven gates

steps.name: Eligibility
steps.text: Qualification, certification, experience and prerequisites are met.

steps.name: Readiness
steps.text: Competencies for the **target** role — not only success in the current one.

steps.name: Need
steps.text: An approved role, vacancy or network need exists.

steps.name: Selection
steps.text: The authorised process, completed fairly and consistently.

steps.name: Appointment
steps.text: Reporting line, scope, allowance / hours and start date formally confirmed.

steps.name: Transition Review
steps.text: Induction, coaching and an early review in the new role.

check: Eligibility → Evidence → Readiness → Organizational Need → Selection → Appointment → Transition Review
Years of service, informal influence, or participation in training alone do not bypass these gates

blocks.title: Fair decisions
do: Use the **same minimum expectations** for the same role across schools.
Make decisions **explainable** through evidence and role requirements.
Check approval, level and hours in the **Role Register**.
dont: Promise a role, allowance or teaching-hour reduction that is not in the Role Register.
Use protected or irrelevant personal characteristics in selection.
Treat an old job description as current authority.
check: Career decisions should be explainable through evidence and role requirements
Protected or irrelevant personal characteristics must not be used in selection decisions

blocks.title: Common questions

items.q: I have taught here for many years. Do I qualify for the next role?
items.a: Years of service alone never create an entitlement. Every move passes the seven gates — eligibility, evidence, readiness, organisational need, selection, appointment and a transition review.

items.q: Does a strong appraisal result mean promotion?
items.a: No. Formal appraisal evidence may support a readiness decision, but strong performance alone does not create an entitlement. There must also be readiness for the target role and an approved need.

items.q: Can a school create a new coordinator role with reduced teaching hours?
items.a: Not on its own. Role approval, level, classification and teaching-hour / allowance values come from the Role Register. A local job description may add detail but can never create a new role, level, allowance or hour reduction.

items.q: Is a Subject Specialist the manager of our Heads of Department?
items.a: No. The HOD manages the subject inside the school's line structure. The Subject Specialist supports and reviews subject quality across schools without replacing local line management.
